title: Canonical constant and inverse-limit coefficient comparisons under pro-etale inverse image
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Use their small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the inverse-image functor $f^{-1}$, and the canonical maps $c^f_R:f^{-1}R_Y\to R_X$ adjoint to constant sections, from [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]; here $R_Z$ denotes the sheafification of the constant ring presheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Define $c^f$ as the natural transformation from $R\mapsto f^{-1}R_Y$ to $R\mapsto R_X$ with component $c^f_R$. For any countable diagram $Q:\mathbf N^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{CRing}_{u+1}$, with $X,Y:\mathrm{Scheme}_u$, define $T_Z(Q)=Q\circ(-)_Z$, the diagram of constant ring sheaves. Define $c^f_Q:f^{-1}(\varprojlim T_Y(Q))\to\varprojlim T_X(Q)$ to be the universal limit comparison $f^{-1}\varprojlim T_Y(Q)\to\varprojlim(f^{-1}T_Y(Q))$, followed by the limit map induced by the natural transformation with components $c^f_{Q_n}$. This defines the specific map for every such diagram, without requiring finite rings, surjective transition maps, limit preservation or invertibility of $c^f_Q$.
